name: Mirvel Sorrel-Pomegranate Bloom
description: A premium botanical soda using real sorrel (hibiscus sabdariffa) and real pomegranate extract, lightly sweetened and finely carbonated, positioned as a sophisticated alternative to mainstream fruit sodas. The deep ruby color is natural and part of the brand identity.
flavor_profile: Tart sorrel brightness, pomegranate depth and mild tannin, floral hibiscus undertone, elegant dry finish
cultural_context: Mirvel Sorrel-Pomegranate Bloom is a fixture at Tier 3 dinner tables and Tier 4 casual settings — the drink you bring to a gathering when you want to signal taste without showing off. It's poured into proper glassware, photographed, and associated with a certain aspirational but understated aesthetic. Real-extract at this price point is a statement of values as much as a beverage choice.
story_hooks: Mirvel's sorrel supply comes from a single regional co-op whose members are being squeezed by a land acquisition — if the co-op fails, Mirvel either reformulates with synth or ceases to exist as currently constituted.

A high-profile poisoning at a Tier 4 event is initially linked to the Mirvel Sorrel-Pomegranate served that evening — the company is innocent but the investigation is damaging and someone seems to be steering it deliberately.

A Tier 3 sommelier who built her reputation on Mirvel pairings discovers that the 'real extract' certification may have been falsified for the last two production runs — she has to decide what to do with that information.
related_entities: Tessera Corponation ChronoMark VR-3 Passive Isotopic Citizen Tagging System
